result.summary: Security HARD GATE re-review (Step 2c rework 2) for PRM-02..05 promotion pipeline: PASS. Re-reviewed the full production diff since the rework1 PASS commit (3be9639b) — TEST-DESIGNER's Step 3 changes: Zig 0.16 compile fixes (std.json .items, ArrayList API migration, fillRandom replacing removed std.crypto.random), genuine bug fixes (segfault from freeing a string literal on the timestampToIso path, getReview off-by-one column indices, 5x fmtInt leaks, errdefer->defer leak in rejectIfConflicts), and design-required source-status guards on all five transition UPDATEs. INV-1: guards run under the single owner-tenant search_path (rework1 decision unchanged), promotion_reviews still per-tenant only (no migration/BUSINESS_TABLES change in diff). INV-2: guards fail-closed on 0 rows (InvalidReviewTransition); no client-supplied identity path added. INV-7: all SQL parameterised ($N); status literals are server-side constants; lint_sql_param_types exit 0; no allocPrint SQL interpolation in diff. INV-8: no catch unreachable in diff. INV-3/INV-4/INV-5 not applicable. getReview column fix verified correct for the 14-column SELECT (indices 0-13); rejectIfConflicts defer-frees verified not to double-free (ConflictRejection return does not alias payload/idem_key). Verified: zig build check exit 0, lint_migration_schema exit 0, lint_sql_table_refs exit 0. Two MINOR non-invariant observations (timestampToIso now returns a fixed epoch placeholder — functional regression, not a security issue; fillRandom ignores getrandom return — robustness nit mirroring onboarding.zig). TEST-RUNNER (Step 4) may start.

issues.description: timestampToIso now returns a fixed '1970-01-01T00:00:00Z' placeholder, so `created_at` in the promotion-context response (handleGetPromotionContext) is no longer the review's creation time. Pre-existing code was equally broken (dangling stack-buffer pointer + free-on-string-literal segfault); the fix removes the crash but leaves the field constant. Not an INV-1..INV-8 violation (server-populated field, no unauthorised data, no authorisation signal). Recommend a follow-up for real ISO formatting (code comment already carries the TODO).

fillRandom ignores the return value of std.os.linux.getrandom; on Linux a failure would leave uuid_bytes undefined. Impact bounded: bytes only feed a synthetic `promotion_id` used as an event idempotency key, not an access-control token; getrandom(2) for 16 bytes blocks rather than fails on entropy starvation; all platforms use a CSPRNG (getrandom / RtlGenRandom / arc4random_buf); mirrors the pre-existing onboarding.zig fillRandom pattern. Not a security-invariant violation.
